candidates.title: File:Devastation in Asheville after Hurricane Helene.jpg
candidates.author: Bill McMannis
candidates.description: Hurricane Helene caused widespread devastation in Western North Carolina. This picture I took Friday a half block from my house. The dam at the WNC Nature Center on the Swannanoa River was ripped apart. My house has a tree on it and three came down in my driveway but we are okay and the damage to the house s minimal. Water will likely be unavailable for two to four weeks. The hope is power will be restored Friday. Uploading this picture is the first internet related task I have been able to do since Thursday. I gave some videos, but cannot upload

candidates.author: Bill McMannis
candidates.description: Balda Baldessa and Zeiss Ikon Contessa were mid-50’s W. German rangefinder cameras aimed at the same market. Balda competed being less expensive and Zeiss competed on quality. Functionally, they were similar: 45mm f/2.8 lenses, uncoupled light meters and both are compact enough to fit in your coat pocket. Both take very nice images. Both examples are fully functional including the light meters.

candidates.title: File:Devastation in Asheville after Hurricane Helene.jpg
candidates.author: Bill McMannis
candidates.description: Hurricane Helene caused widespread devastation in Western North Carolina. This picture I took Friday a half block from my house. The dam at the WNC Nature Center on the Swannanoa River was ripped apart. My house has a tree on it and three came down in my driveway but we are okay and the damage to the house s minimal. Water will likely be unavailable for two to four weeks. The hope is power will be restored Friday. Uploading this picture is the first internet related task I have been able to do since Thursday. I gave some videos, but cannot upload

candidates.title: File:Burlington City Park Menagerie Carousel - Carved Dentzel Cats.jpg
candidates.author: Chris Laforet
candidates.description: Burlington NC hosts one of the about 20 remaining Dentzel carousels. It was built around 1906-1910 and is known as a "menagerie carousel" because of its rich array of animals. This carousel has three rows and a perfectly functioning band organ. Dentzel's were well known for their incredible realism in their carvings, showing muscles and even veins where appropriate. The eyes are made of glass and the tails of real horsehair. This is an image of a place or building that is listed on the National Register of Historic Places in the United States of America . Its reference number is 82003420 ( Wikidata ).

candidates.title: File:Crossing Curb Cut St albans L7 Davidson (6124624424).jpg
candidates.author: Brett VA
candidates.description: This front loaded home has an excellent setback for the garage minimizing the impact of parking and curb cuts on walkability. The utilities are buried which saves the street trees from being hacked away by the power company. Note the ugly utility box on the right. Even with all this good design rear loading is just better. candidates.title: File:Mighty Mushroom—Pilobolus kleinii Shoots its Spores at the Sun.jpg
candidates.author: Akulshres
candidates.description: Pilobolus is a unique genus of mushrooms which facilitates spore dispersal through an incredible, fast-based mechanism. The sporangium—the small black structure atop the mushroom body—is fired off at 20,000g. This acceleration is faster than the space shuttle and faster than a missle. In fact, it is the fastest natural acceleration ever recorded, currently holding the world record. This is quantitatively the fastest flight on Earth.

candidates.title: File:Views at Guilford Courthouse National Military Park, North Carolina (0a5d0573-625e-44fe-ac24-30418538fcee).jpg
candidates.author: NPS staff
candidates.description: Historical interpretive presentations on battle at Guilford Courthouse during Revolutionary War. The battle fought here on March 15, 1781, was the largest, most hotly-contested action of the Revolutionary Wars climactic Southern Campaign. The serious loss of British manpower suffered at Guilford Courthouse foreshadowed Lord Cornwallis final defeat at Yorktown seven months later. Keywords: guco; National military parks; American history; Revolutionary War; 1775-1783; Greene; Nathanael; 1742-1786.; Military history

candidates.title: File:Bill Clinton Visits High Point University (3347069698).jpg
candidates.author: Harris Walker from Currently Living in Washington, DC for a Summer Internship, USA
candidates.description: While campaigning for wife Hillary in her campaign for President, Bill Clinton stopped in the Triad to speak to the students of High Point University. What I love so much about these pictures is the way there was no way to take them without the Secret Service agent being in them. It's very representative of the duty of these agents, though, so I like it because it adds to the picture, though kind of taking away from the composition.

candidates.title: File:1953 High Point, NC Soap Box Derby racer Henry Clyde Williams, Jr.jpg
candidates.author: Bill Wrigley
candidates.description: This is a Soap Box Derby racer driven by Henry Clyde Williams, Jr. (1937-2022) who took 2nd place in the High Point, NC local race in 1953. Clyde ran as a class A entry at the age of 15, his last year of entry in the Derby. It was the centerpiece of an exhibit entitled The Need for Speed: Soap Box Derby Racing in High Point, which opened February 2023 and ran through March.

candidates.author: Bill Wrigley
candidates.description: This is a Soap Box Derby racer driven by Henry Clyde Williams, Jr. (1937-2022) who took 2nd place in the High Point, NC local race in 1953. Clyde ran as a class A entry at the age of 15, his last year of entry in the Derby. It was the centerpiece of an exhibit entitled The Need for Speed: Soap Box Derby Racing in High Point, which opened February 2023 and ran through March.

candidates.description: A carriage house accessory dwelling unit off of "Fran and Kukla Alley". The developer of the project is quite a punster with alley names. Also nearby is "Alley of the Dolls" Note the deep setback the garage has from the alley to accomodate underground utility right of way. rear loaded utilities allows homes to be built closer to the street for a better walkable environment. This photo was taken a week before the 2011 superbowl. Clearly, this resident was happy with the outcome. candidates.title: File:President James K. Polk Birthplace, Pineville, North Carolina (47490957132).jpg
candidates.author: Ken Lund from Reno, Nevada, USA
candidates.description: James Knox Polk (November 2, 1795 – June 15, 1849) was the 11th president of the United States, serving from 1845 to 1849. He previously was Speaker of the House of Representatives (1835–1839) and Governor of Tennessee (1839–1841). A protégé of Andrew Jackson, he was a member of the Democratic Party and an advocate of Jacksonian democracy. Polk is chiefly known for extending the territory of the United States through the Mexican–American War; during his presidency, the United States expanded significantly with the annexation of the Republic of Texas, the Oregon Territory, and the Mexican Cession following the American victory in the Mexican–American War. After building a successful law practice in Tennessee, Polk was elected to the state legislature (1823) and then to the United States House of Representatives in 1825, becoming a strong supporter of Andrew Jackson. After serving as chairman of the Ways and Means Committee, he became Speaker in 1835, the only president to have been Speaker. Polk left Congress to run for governor of Tennessee; he won in 1839, but lost in 1841 and 1843. He was a dark horse candidate for the Democratic nomination for president in 1844; he entered his party's convention as a potential nominee for vice president, but emerged as a compromise to head the ticket when no presidential candidate could secure the necessary two-thirds majority. In the general election, Polk defeated Henry Clay of the rival Whig Party. Historians have praised Polk for having met during his four-year term every major domestic and foreign policy goal he had set. After a negotiation fraught with risk of war, he reached a settlement with Great Britain over the disputed Oregon Country, the territory for the most part being divided along the 49th parallel. Polk achieved a sweeping victory in the Mexican–American War, which resulted in the cession by Mexico of nearly all the American Southwest. He secured a substantial reduction of tariff rates with the Walker tariff of 1846. The same year, he achieved his other major goal, re-establishment of the Independent Treasury system. Historian Thomas A. Bailey says that during the Mexican war, "Polk was an energetic and indefatigable war leader, and he emerged, partly through rare good luck, with uninterrupted success. He kept the sole direction of the war in his own hands, from grand strategy to the procurement of mules." True to his campaign pledge to serve only one term, Polk left office in 1849 and returned to Tennessee, where he died three months after leaving the White House. Though relatively obscure today, scholars have ranked Polk favorably for his ability to promote and achieve the major items on his presidential agenda, despite limiting himself to a single term. However, he has also been criticized for leading the country into an aggressive war against Mexico and thus exacerbating divides between free and slave states. An owner of property who used slave labor for most of his adult life, he owned a plantation in Mississippi and increased his slave ownership while president. The prime legacy of Polk's presidency of territorial expansion – with the United States reaching the Pacific coast and, roughly, its present contiguous borders – was a nation poised to become a world power, but with sectional divisions gravely exacerbated. Tensions between pro- and anti-slave settlers in the conquered west (not limited to Bleeding Kansas) and the bid to constitute newfound states as either free or slave – and thus for control of the senate – set the stage for the Civil War, considered a direct consequence of Polk's presidency. a href=" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_K._Polk " rel="noreferrer nofollow" en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_K._Polk /a a href=" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Text_of_Creative_Commons_Attribution-ShareAlike_3.0_Unported_License " rel="noreferrer nofollow" en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Text_of_Creative_Commons_... /a

After serving as chairman of the Ways and Means Committee, he became Speaker in 1835, the only president to have been Speaker. Polk left Congress to run for governor of Tennessee; he won in 1839, but lost in 1841 and 1843. He was a dark horse candidate for the Democratic nomination for president in 1844; he entered his party's convention as a potential nominee for vice president, but emerged as a compromise to head the ticket when no presidential candidate could secure the necessary two-thirds majority. In the general election, Polk defeated Henry Clay of the rival Whig Party. Historians have praised Polk for having met during his four-year term every major domestic and foreign policy goal he had set. After a negotiation fraught with risk of war, he reached a settlement with Great Britain over the disputed Oregon Country, the territory for the most part being divided along the 49th parallel. Polk achieved a sweeping victory in the Mexican–American War, which resulted in the cession by Mexico of nearly all the American Southwest. He secured a substantial reduction of tariff rates with the Walker tariff of 1846. The same year, he achieved his other major goal, re-establishment of the Independent Treasury system. Historian Thomas A. Bailey says that during the Mexican war, "Polk was an energetic and indefatigable war leader, and he emerged, partly through rare good luck, with uninterrupted success. He kept the sole direction of the war in his own hands, from grand strategy to the procurement of mules." True to his campaign pledge to serve only one term, Polk left office in 1849 and returned to Tennessee, where he died three months after leaving the White House. Though relatively obscure today, scholars have ranked Polk favorably for his ability to promote and achieve the major items on his presidential agenda, despite limiting himself to a single term. However, he has also been criticized for leading the country into an aggressive war against Mexico and thus exacerbating divides between free and slave states. An owner of property who used slave labor for most of his adult life, he owned a plantation in Mississippi and increased his slave ownership while president. The prime legacy of Polk's presidency of territorial expansion – with the United States reaching the Pacific coast and, roughly, its present contiguous borders – was a nation poised to become a world power, but with sectional divisions gravely exacerbated. Tensions between pro- and anti-slave settlers in the conquered west (not limited to Bleeding Kansas) and the bid to constitute newfound states as either free or slave – and thus for control of the senate – set the stage for the Civil War, considered a direct consequence of Polk's presidency. a href=" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_K._Polk " rel="noreferrer nofollow" en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_K._Polk /a a href=" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Text_of_Creative_Commons_Attribution-ShareAlike_3.0_Unported_License " rel="noreferrer nofollow" en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Text_of_Creative_Commons_... /a

candidates.title: File:History Neglect (1593321670).jpg
candidates.author: Wendy
candidates.description: This is a series of 20 pictures of the W.E.B. DuBois School in Wake Forest NC Wider shot of the building that housed the music,art and band rooms. You can see the stack still standing in the rear left - the old parts of the school had floor radiators for heat. None of the school had AC. The W.E.B. DuBois School opened in 1926 in the African-American community in Wake Forest, North Carolina. In 1939 it became the Wake Forest Colored High School and in 1971 was integrated and served as the campus of the Wake Forest-Rolesville Middle School. When that school outgrew the facility and moved to its present location on South Main Street in 1989, the DuBois campus became vacant. For 10 years the campus was abandoned until the DuBois Alumni Association purchased it from the Wake County School System. The two oldest buildings are in such disrepair that they are falling down. The sixth and seventh grade buildings are boarded up but are in poor condition. The eighth grade and vocational buildings continue to deteriorate almost to a point beyond repair. The gym and shop buildings are being used as community centers.

candidates.title: File:2019 Wilson County Court House, Wilson, North Carolina.jpg
candidates.author: Beyond My Ken
candidates.description: The Wilson County Court House at 115 Nash Street E in Wilson, North Carolina was built in 1925-25, replacing a brick court house on the same site that had been built in 1855 and re-modeled in 1902. The current courthouse was designed by Fred A. Bishop in the neo-Classical style. The building was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1979.

candidates.title: File:Soldiers' monument, Wilson, North Carolina.jpg
candidates.author: Beyond My Ken
candidates.description: This soldiers' monument stands at the corner of Nash and Goldsboro Streets in Wilson, North Carolina, to the right of the Wilson County Court House. The plaque in front reads: "TO THE / VALOR / OF WILSON COUNTY / SOLDIERS". On the back of the monument is inscribed: "ERECTED BY / THE JOHN W. DUNHAM CHAPTER U.D.C. / AND / THE THOMAS HADLEY CHAPTER D.A.R. // NOVEMBER 11, 1926". ("U.D.C." is "United Daughters of the Confederacy", and "D.A.R." is "Daughters of the American Revolution".)

candidates.title: File:Whirligig (14) (24150028249).jpg
candidates.author: Gerry Dincher from Hope Mills, NC
candidates.description: The Vollis Simpson Whirligig Park is at 301 Goldsboro Street in Wilson, North Carolina. It really is something to see. Wilson is a few miles of Interstate 95 in eastern North Carolina.

candidates.title: File:Whirligig Park, Wilson, North Carolina 01.jpg
candidates.author: Beyond My Ken
candidates.description: The Vollis Simpson Whirliigig Park on Goldsboro Street S. at Douglas Street S. in Wilson, North Carolina, opened on November 2, 2017 to document, conserve, and display the large whirlgigs from Simpson's property in Lucama, North Carolina. Wilson held its first annual Wilson Whirligig Festival in 2004. It was renamed in 2016 to the North Carolina Whirligig Festival, and is usually held the first full weekend of November. The North Carolina legislature named the whirligig the state's official folk art in June 2013.
